subject: chemistry
note: One revision note per concept. Each GCSE spec point is primary in exactly one concept; non-primary refs are broad points that also need this note.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Atoms, elements, compounds and formulae
concepts.scope: What atoms, elements and compounds are, and how chemical symbols and formulae represent them.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Mixtures and separation techniques
concepts.scope: What a mixture is and how filtration, crystallisation, simple and fractional distillation separate mixtures, and how to choose a method.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Development of the model of the atom
concepts.scope: How the atomic model changed from Dalton to Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr and Chadwick as new evidence appeared.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Subatomic particles and the size of atoms
concepts.scope: Protons, neutrons and electrons: their charges, masses and positions, why atoms are neutral, and the size of atoms and nuclei.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Atomic number, mass number and isotopes
concepts.scope: Using atomic and mass numbers to count protons, neutrons and electrons in atoms and ions, and what isotopes are.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Relative atomic mass
concepts.scope: Why relative atomic masses are averages and how to calculate one from isotope masses and abundances.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Electronic structure
concepts.scope: How electrons fill shells for the first 20 elements and how electron arrangement links to group and period.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Development of the periodic table
concepts.scope: How Mendeleev arranged the elements, left gaps and predicted new ones, and how atomic number fixed the anomalies.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: The modern periodic table
concepts.scope: How elements are arranged by atomic number into groups and periods, and how position predicts reactions.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Metals and non-metals
concepts.scope: Where metals and non-metals sit in the periodic table and how their properties and ion formation differ.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Group 1: the alkali metals
concepts.scope: Properties of the alkali metals, their reactions with water, and why reactivity increases down the group.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Group 7: the halogens
concepts.scope: Properties and trends of the halogens, their reactions with metals and hydrogen, and displacement reactions as redox.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Group 0: the noble gases
concepts.scope: Why the noble gases are unreactive, the trends in their physical properties and how their uses follow from them.

concepts.group: Atomic structure and the periodic table
concepts.title: Transition metals
concepts.scope: Properties of transition metals compared with Group 1: ions of different charge, coloured compounds and catalytic activity.

concepts.title: States of matter and changes of state
concepts.scope: The particle model of solids, liquids and gases, changes of state, predicting states from data and the limits of the model.

concepts.title: Chemical bonds and types of structure
concepts.scope: Overview of ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, how to classify substances by structure, and the limitations of bonding models.

concepts.title: Ionic bonding
concepts.scope: How metal and non-metal atoms transfer electrons to form ions, shown with dot-and-cross diagrams.

concepts.title: Ionic compounds: structure and formulae
concepts.scope: The giant ionic lattice and how to work out formulae and names of ionic compounds from their ions.

concepts.title: Properties of ionic compounds
concepts.scope: Why ionic compounds have high melting points and conduct only when molten or dissolved.

concepts.title: Covalent bonding and dot-and-cross diagrams
concepts.scope: How shared electron pairs form covalent bonds and molecules, drawn as dot-and-cross diagrams.

concepts.title: Properties of simple molecular substances
concepts.scope: Why small molecules have low melting and boiling points and do not conduct, in terms of intermolecular forces.

concepts.title: Polymer structure
concepts.scope: How polymers are long chains held by strong covalent bonds, and why they are solids at room temperature.

concepts.title: Giant covalent structures: diamond, graphite and silicon dioxide
concepts.scope: The structures of diamond, graphite and silicon dioxide and how they explain hardness, high melting points and conductivity.

concepts.title: Graphene and fullerenes
concepts.scope: The structures, properties and uses of graphene, buckminsterfullerene and carbon nanotubes.

concepts.title: Metallic bonding and properties of metals
concepts.scope: The sea of delocalised electrons and how it explains high melting points, malleability and conductivity of metals.

concepts.title: Nanoparticles
concepts.scope: The size of nanoparticles, their high surface area to volume ratio, their uses and their possible risks.

concepts.title: Word, balanced and ionic equations
concepts.scope: Writing word equations, balanced symbol equations with state symbols, and balanced ionic equations.

concepts.title: Conservation of mass
concepts.scope: The law of conservation of mass, and why mass seems to change when a gas is given off or taken in.

concepts.title: Relative formula mass and percentage by mass
concepts.scope: Calculating Mr from relative atomic masses and the percentage by mass of an element in a compound.

concepts.title: Empirical and molecular formulae
concepts.scope: Working out empirical formulae from reacting masses or percentages, the link to molecular formulae, and the magnesium oxide experiment.

concepts.title: The mole and the Avogadro constant
concepts.scope: The mole as a fixed number of particles and converting between mass, moles and number of particles.

concepts.title: Reacting masses from equations
concepts.scope: Using a balanced equation and moles to calculate the mass of a reactant or product.

concepts.title: Using moles to balance equations
concepts.scope: Deducing the balancing numbers (stoichiometry) of an equation from the masses of reactants and products.

concepts.title: Limiting reactants
concepts.scope: Why the reactant that is used up limits the amount of product, and calculations with an excess reactant.

concepts.title: Concentration in g/dm³
concepts.scope: Calculating concentration as mass of solute per volume of solution, and what dilute and concentrated mean.

concepts.title: Concentration in mol/dm³
concepts.scope: Calculating concentration in mol/dm³ and converting between g/dm³ and mol/dm³.

concepts.title: Titration calculations
concepts.scope: Using titration results to calculate an unknown concentration or volume of solution.

concepts.title: Percentage yield
concepts.scope: Why actual yield is less than theoretical yield, and calculating theoretical mass and percentage yield.

concepts.title: Atom economy
concepts.scope: Calculating atom economy and using it with yield, rate and cost to choose a reaction pathway.

concepts.title: Molar gas volume
concepts.scope: Using 24 dm³ per mole at room temperature and pressure to calculate volumes of gases in reactions.

concepts.title: Oxidation and reduction (oxygen)
concepts.scope: Metals reacting with oxygen, and oxidation and reduction as gain and loss of oxygen.

concepts.title: The reactivity series
concepts.scope: Ordering metals by their reactions with water and acids, and how reactivity relates to forming positive ions and resisting oxidation.

concepts.title: Extraction of metals by reduction with carbon
concepts.scope: Why unreactive metals occur native and how metals below carbon are extracted from ores by reduction.

concepts.title: Redox in terms of electrons
concepts.scope: Oxidation and reduction as loss and gain of electrons, ionic equations for displacement reactions, and spectator ions.

concepts.title: Acids, alkalis and the pH scale
concepts.scope: Hydrogen and hydroxide ions, the pH scale, and the colours of common indicators.

concepts.title: Strong and weak acids
concepts.scope: Strong versus weak acids by degree of ionisation, dilute versus concentrated, and how pH changes by one unit per factor of 10 in hydrogen ion concentration.

concepts.title: Neutralisation, bases and salts
concepts.scope: Bases and alkalis, neutralisation as H+ + OH- giving water, and how to name the salt formed.

concepts.title: Reactions of acids with metals and carbonates
concepts.scope: The products of acids reacting with metals and carbonates, with balanced equations and the redox view.

concepts.title: Required practical: making a soluble salt
concepts.scope: Preparing a pure, dry soluble salt (eg copper sulfate) from an acid and an insoluble base, and when titration is needed instead.

concepts.title: Solubility rules and making insoluble salts
concepts.scope: The solubility rules for common compounds, predicting precipitates, and preparing a pure, dry insoluble salt.

concepts.title: Practical: pH change during neutralisation
concepts.scope: Measuring pH with indicator or a pH meter while adding a base such as calcium hydroxide to an acid.

concepts.title: Required practical: acid-alkali titration
concepts.scope: Carrying out an accurate titration with burette, pipette and indicator to find reacting volumes.

concepts.title: The process of electrolysis
concepts.scope: What electrolytes are and how ions move to the electrodes when a direct current passes through.

concepts.title: Electrolysis of molten ionic compounds
concepts.scope: Predicting the products at each electrode when a molten binary ionic compound is electrolysed.

concepts.title: Electrolysis of aqueous solutions
concepts.scope: Why hydrogen or the metal forms at the cathode and oxygen or a halogen at the anode when solutions are electrolysed.

concepts.title: Half equations at the electrodes
concepts.scope: Writing half equations for electrode reactions and recognising reduction at the cathode and oxidation at the anode.

concepts.title: Extracting aluminium by electrolysis
concepts.scope: Why reactive metals are extracted by electrolysis and how aluminium is made from molten aluminium oxide and cryolite.

concepts.title: Practical: electrolysis of copper sulfate solution
concepts.scope: Electrolysing copper sulfate with inert and with copper electrodes, and how copper electrodes purify copper.

concepts.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
concepts.scope: How reactions transfer energy to or from the surroundings, with everyday examples of each.

concepts.title: Practical: temperature changes in reactions
concepts.scope: Measuring temperature changes for dissolving, neutralisation, displacement and precipitation to classify reactions.

concepts.title: Reaction profiles and activation energy
concepts.scope: Drawing and labelling reaction profiles for exothermic and endothermic reactions and explaining activation energy.

concepts.title: Bond energies
concepts.scope: Bond breaking as endothermic and bond making as exothermic, and calculating energy changes from bond energies.

concepts.title: Practical: combustion of alcohols (calorimetry)
concepts.scope: Comparing the temperature rise in water produced by burning different alcohols.

concepts.title: Hydrogen as a fuel for cars
concepts.scope: Advantages and disadvantages of using hydrogen rather than petrol as a car fuel.

concepts.title: Chemical cells and batteries
concepts.scope: How cells produce a voltage from reactions, what affects the voltage, and why non-rechargeable cells run out.

concepts.title: Fuel cells
concepts.scope: How a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell works and how it compares with rechargeable batteries.

concepts.title: Measuring and calculating rates of reaction
concepts.scope: Calculating mean rate and rate from the gradient of a graph of product or reactant against time.

concepts.title: Practical: investigating rates of reaction
concepts.scope: Measuring rate by gas volume, mass loss or colour change and turbidity, and investigating the effect of changing conditions.

concepts.title: Factors affecting the rate of reaction
concepts.scope: How concentration, pressure, surface area, temperature and catalysts change the rate of reaction.

concepts.title: Collision theory and activation energy
concepts.scope: Explaining the effect of each factor on rate through the frequency and energy of collisions.

concepts.title: Catalysts and enzymes
concepts.scope: How catalysts speed up reactions by providing a route with lower activation energy, and enzymes as biological catalysts.

concepts.title: Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
concepts.scope: Reversible reactions, their energy changes in each direction, and dynamic equilibrium in a closed system.

concepts.title: Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.scope: How changing concentration, temperature or pressure shifts the position of equilibrium.

concepts.title: Crude oil, hydrocarbons and alkanes
concepts.scope: Crude oil as a finite mixture of hydrocarbons, and the formulae and structures of the first four alkanes.

concepts.title: Homologous series and functional groups
concepts.scope: What a homologous series is, how functional groups decide reactions, and naming the first four members of each series.

concepts.title: Fractional distillation of crude oil
concepts.scope: How crude oil is separated into fractions and the names and uses of the main fractions.

concepts.title: Properties and combustion of hydrocarbons
concepts.scope: How chain length affects boiling point, viscosity and flammability, and the complete combustion of hydrocarbons.

concepts.title: Cracking
concepts.scope: Breaking large alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes by catalytic or steam cracking, and why it is needed.

concepts.title: Alkenes: structure and reactions
concepts.scope: The C=C functional group, the bromine water test and addition reactions with hydrogen, water and halogens.

concepts.title: Alcohols
concepts.scope: Structures and reactions of the first four alcohols, oxidation to carboxylic acids, and making ethanol by fermentation.

concepts.title: Carboxylic acids
concepts.scope: Structures and properties of the first four carboxylic acids as weak acids and their reactions.

concepts.title: Addition polymerisation
concepts.scope: How alkene monomers join to make addition polymers, drawing repeating units, and linking polymer uses to properties.

concepts.title: Condensation polymerisation
concepts.scope: How monomers with two functional groups join to form polyesters and lose a small molecule such as water.

concepts.title: Natural polymers: amino acids, proteins and DNA
concepts.scope: Amino acids forming proteins, and DNA, starch, cellulose as naturally occurring polymers.

concepts.title: Pure substances and melting points
concepts.scope: What pure means in chemistry, and using sharp melting and boiling points to identify pure substances.

concepts.title: Formulations
concepts.scope: Formulations as mixtures designed with measured amounts of each component for a purpose.

concepts.title: Required practical: chromatography
concepts.scope: Paper and thin-layer chromatography, stationary and mobile phases, Rf values, and investigating the composition of inks.

concepts.title: Tests for gases
concepts.scope: The tests for hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, chlorine and ammonia.

concepts.title: Flame tests
concepts.scope: Identifying lithium, sodium, potassium, calcium and copper ions from their flame colours, and how to do the test.

concepts.title: Metal hydroxide precipitate tests
concepts.scope: Identifying metal ions from the colour of precipitates formed with sodium hydroxide solution.

concepts.title: Tests for carbonate, halide and sulfate ions
concepts.scope: Identifying anions using dilute acid, acidified silver nitrate and acidified barium chloride.

concepts.title: Required practical: identifying ions in an unknown salt
concepts.scope: Combining cation and anion tests to identify an unknown ionic compound, and why each test must be unique.

concepts.title: Instrumental methods and flame emission spectroscopy
concepts.scope: Advantages of instrumental analysis and interpreting flame emission spectra and flame photometer data.

concepts.title: Earth's atmosphere: composition and evolution
concepts.scope: Today's atmosphere and how the early volcanic atmosphere changed as oceans formed and plants produced oxygen.

concepts.title: Greenhouse gases and the greenhouse effect
concepts.scope: How carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour absorb and re-emit infrared radiation to keep Earth warm.

concepts.title: Human activity and climate change: the evidence
concepts.scope: Human activities that add greenhouse gases and how to evaluate the evidence that they cause climate change.

concepts.title: Effects of climate change and the carbon footprint
concepts.scope: The potential effects of global warming, the carbon footprint and ways to reduce it.

concepts.title: Carbon monoxide and particulates from incomplete combustion
concepts.scope: How incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and soot, and why they are harmful.

concepts.title: Sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and acid rain
concepts.scope: How sulfur impurities and high engine temperatures produce sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, and their effects including acid rain.

concepts.title: Sustainability: reduce, reuse and recycle
concepts.scope: Using finite resources sustainably, and the benefits and problems of recycling metals, glass and polymers.

concepts.title: Potable water and waste water treatment
concepts.scope: Making drinking water from fresh water and seawater, and how sewage and waste water are treated.

concepts.title: Biological methods of metal extraction
concepts.scope: Phytomining and bioleaching as ways to extract metals such as copper from low-grade ores.

concepts.title: Life cycle assessment
concepts.scope: The stages of a life cycle assessment and how to interpret and evaluate LCA data for products.

concepts.title: Corrosion and its prevention
concepts.scope: Rusting as oxidation, the conditions needed, and prevention by barriers, sacrificial protection and electroplating.

concepts.title: Alloys
concepts.scope: Why alloys are harder than pure metals, common alloys such as steels, brass and bronze, and matching metals to uses.

concepts.title: Ceramics, polymers and composites
concepts.scope: Making and comparing glass, clay ceramics, thermosetting and thermosoftening polymers and composites, and choosing materials for uses.

concepts.title: The Haber process
concepts.scope: Making ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen, the conditions used and how unreacted gases are recycled.

concepts.title: Choosing conditions for industrial processes
concepts.scope: The compromise between rate, equilibrium yield and cost when choosing temperature, pressure and catalyst.

concepts.title: NPK fertilisers
concepts.scope: Why plants need nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, and making fertilisers in the lab and industrially.

concepts.title: Hazard symbols and risk assessment
concepts.scope: Reading hazard symbols and evaluating risks and precautions in practical work.

concepts.title: Uncertainty in measurements
concepts.scope: Using the range of repeat results about the mean to estimate uncertainty.
